candidates.author: Albert Camus
candidates.locator: chapter 1, The Rebel, the closing sentence, p. 28 (Penguin with Hamish Hamilton)
candidates.whyThisMonth: Camus puts rebellion where Descartes put thought and calls it the first clue found in our daily trials: a reader braced for another hard day is told the refusal itself is what binds them to everyone else.

candidates.quote: Dance, when you’re broken open. / Dance, if you’ve torn the bandage off. / Dance in the middle of the fighting.
candidates.author: Rumi
candidates.locator: chapter 27, The Turn: Dance in Your Blood, the poem beginning Dance, when you’re broken open, lines 1 to 3, p. 281
candidates.year: Masnavi, Book III, composed c. 1265; this English 1995
candidates.whyThisMonth: Not dance once the trouble is over but dance inside it: the shortest instruction in the month for someone who has to get up and go on before anything has been resolved.

candidates.quote: Do not go gentle into that good night.
candidates.author: Dylan Thomas
candidates.work: Do not go gentle into that good night
candidates.locator: line 1, first printed in Botteghe Oscure VIII (1951), collected in Collected Poems 1934–1952 (Dent, 1952)
candidates.whyThisMonth: An order not to yield quietly, which is the whole month in seven words: the line itself names no deathbed, though the poem behind it is addressed to a dying father, and that is the publishability call to make.

candidates.quote: Against the assault of laughter nothing can stand.
candidates.author: Mark Twain
candidates.speaker: Satan
candidates.whyThisMonth: Satan tells the boys the one weapon they own and never use is laughter: for a reader facing something that looks immovable, a reminder that the thing may only be a humbug.

candidates.quote: Whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul … then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can.
candidates.author: Herman Melville
candidates.speaker: Ishmael
candidates.whyThisMonth: Ishmael names the grey mood exactly and then says what he does about it instead of sitting in it: the quiet end of the theme, the morning where holding on means getting up and moving.

candidates.quote: Music was my refuge. I could crawl into the spaces between the notes and curl my back to loneliness.
candidates.author: Maya Angelou
candidates.work: Singin’ and Swingin’ and Gettin’ Merry Like Christmas
candidates.whyThisMonth: The quietest courage in the month: not defiance but the small shelter a person builds to get through a lonely stretch, and it holds.
